- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥1.0) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% of recent mean or median.
- When sentiment is negative (≤-1.0) or shows strong reversal signals, model often overpredicts; reduce forecast by 1–3% to align with mean reversion bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots in next 5–10 days; apply “lag correction” — reduce forecast by 1–2% per day post-spike.
- If model forecast is consistently below true outcome over 3+ consecutive days, apply “mean reversion bias” — increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day until convergence.
- If sentiment shows strong divergence from price trend (e.g., sentiment bullish but price falling), reduce forecast by 1–2% to avoid sentiment-driven overconfidence.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates volatility in early days; increase first 5–7 days’ forecast by 0.5–1.5% to capture momentum.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to “overfit” to recent sentiment; apply “sentiment smoothing” — average sentiment over 3–5 days before adjusting forecast.
